newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rail not interested in JCI - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rail not interested in JCI - paper.

text.p: Black empowerment group Real Africa Investments Ltd (Rail) has decided not to pursue a deal to acquire Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's controlling stake in JCI Ltd, Business Day newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Don Ncube, chairman of Rail which has long been mooted to be the main contender for the JCI stake which Anglo wants to sell to black interests, said the company had a good relationship with Anglo but had opted not to pursue JCI.
The surge in the share price of JCI, from a low of 28.75 rand last January to 49.25 rand at Tuesday's close, is understood to have made the transaction unprofitable for Rail, the paper said.
Rail's withdrawal leaves the way open for rivals New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail), Capital Alliance and African Renaissance to go after the Anglo stake.
Business Day quoted industry sources saying the JCI deal could be concluded by the end of the year.

It is expected to be similar to the recent deal for industrial conglomerate Johnnic, with Anglo likely to sell a 35 percent interest in JCI to black business. Anglo's total stake in JCI, the country's sixth largest mining company, is 47 percent.

Anglo spokesman Michael Spicer said the transaction was likely to move quickly because the sharp increase in JCI's share price was putting pressure on suitors to do a deal before it became too expensive.
Nail sources said the group would consider buying the entire 35 percent stake for sale by Anglo but would not rule out forming a partnership with other black empowerment groups.
